items.project: the construction and operation of a Freeski and Snowboard Airbag Training Center. The training center is proposed at the former Timber Ridge Ski Area. The existing gravel parking area will be resurfaced but will not be expanded. Four jumps are proposed within existing ski trail cuts, each with a run-in slope, jump and air bag landing. Two magic carpets are proposed from the mountain base to the top of the jumps and underground electric will be installed to the jumps. The jumps will require misting, with water supply from existing non-potable wells on the property and water storage is proposed in an above ground tank

This permit specifically authorizes tree clearing and the construction of a shed and parking area within a newly created building envelope. The shed will not be utilized for commercial activities or connected to any utilities. Both the shed and new parking area will be accessed off the existing driveway, (the “Project”).

This permit specifically authorizes after-the-fact approval for the demolition of an existing single-family home on Lot 2 of the Barstow Acres development, and the subsequent construction of new 4-bedroom single-family home with a 1-bedroom accessory dwelling unit served by an existing well and new septic mound system.

Project generally described as the construction of updated stormwater treatment infrastructure at Sugarwoods residential subdivision in Barre Town to bring the subdivision into compliance with the State mandated 3-Acre Rule. The project involves the construction of a bioretention system to treat stormwater from 2.098 acres of impervious surface. The project includes the construction of a 4’ wide berm with a 5’ wide high-flow spillway with an 8” PVC underdrain carrier pipe to convey discharge to two new catchbasins. A 24” sump will be installed in each basin to trap sediment prior to discharging to a stone outfall with a precast concrete headwall. The system also includes the installation of a new drainage manhole with a 24” frame and grate drain cover and 24” sump, and three new catchbasins with 24” square frame and grate and 24” sumps for conveyance to the system. The bioretention system will be located in a grassed area south of Sugarwoods Road at its northerly intersection with Windy Wood Road, Barre Town, Vermont.

The project is generally described as the installation of a temporary 50’ tall telecommunication monopole on the summit of Mt. Ellen in Fayston, adjacent to the North Ridge Express at the Sugarbush Resort. There will be 9 panel antennas, 2 whip antennas, and 1 microwave disk antenna mounted on the monopole. A utility HVAC walk-up cabinet will be installed at the base of the pole. The installation will be encircled by a 20' x 30' x 8’ metal fence upon which will be mounted numerous public caution/safety signs regarding RF emissions. It is anticipated that the project will require 4 weeks to complete.
applicants: New Cingular Wireless PCS, LLC d/b/a AT&T

items.project: The project is generally described as the construction of a five-story, 65’ x 170’ hotel building with 100 rooms within the existing parking lot in front of the Comfort Inn hotel located at 213 Paine Turnpike N in Berlin, Vermont. A 70-space parking lot will be constructed behind the existing hotel, including 5 designated areas for semitrucks. The project also involves improvements to the on-site stormwater management infrastructure, including the upgrade of an existing wet pond to a gravel wetland and the construction of a new gravel wetland along the northwest boundary of the project tract. Additionally, the existing access drive will be relocated. The project will be served by connections to existing municipal water and wastewater systems.

The project involves the construction of a new stand-alone 80' × 42' (3,360-square-foot) animal wellness center at 236 Riverside Avenue, Lunenburg, Vermont, providing basic veterinary care to low-income community members and those in surrounding communities. The property also contains an existing approximately 3,000-square-foot animal rescue building. The site currently has seven parking spaces. Seven additional spaces will serve the new building, totaling approximately 1,206 square feet. No new lots will be created. Site work will include clearing, grading, excavation, foundation and building construction, utility installation, parking and pedestrian access, final grading, stabilization, landscaping, and restoration. Existing site access will be used; no new public road is proposed. Following construction, the existing animal rescue and new stand-alone animal wellness center will operate on the property. No animals will be housed overnight in the wellness center.

items.project: To construct a new standalone convenience store with separate gasoline and diesel fueling canopies at 4486 Route 5 in the Town of Derby. Stewart’s is under contract to purchase approximately 49,658 square feet of land located at 4518 Route 5 (SPAN #177-056-10120), which is adjacent to the existing convenience store. The existing convenience store and fueling canopies, as well as the structure currently located at 4518 Route 5, will be demolished. A lot line adjustment has been approved by the Town of Derby, allowing the portion of the parcel at 4518 Route 5 to be consolidated with the existing Stewart’s parcel at 4486 Route 5 (SPAN #117-056-11259), creating a single unified property for the proposed development.

The project proposes to construct a five-story, 58,360 square-foot, mixed use building containing 48 units of rental housing, perpetually restricted to household incomes at or below 80% Area Median Income. The project will be located on a 0.6 acre parcel, Lot 3 of a subdivided 6.3 acre parcel, at 125 Lakeside Avenue in Burlington, Vermont. The project will create 7,400 square-feet of non-residential space in the building tentatively planned for a non-profit early education center. Approximately 88% of the gross floor area will be residential, exceeding the required 40% minimum for “mixed use” pursuant to 10 V.S.A. § 6001(28). 100% of the housing units will meet the definition of "affordable housing" pursuant to 10 V.S.A. § 6001(29)(B), exceeding the 20% minimum for "mixed income housing” established under 10 V.S.A. § 6001(27)(B). The project is located entirely within the City of Burlington’s (the City’s) Land Use Review Board (the Board) approved Tier 1B area, see 10 V.S.A § 6081(z)(2), as well as the City’s neighborhood development area. The developer will meet the requirements for a mixed use, mixed income housing project by leasing the units at the limits described in 10 V.S.A. § 6001(27)(B) and 10 V.S.A. § 6001(28). There is no existing Act 250 jurisdiction on the property. According to the United States Census Bureau, the population of the City of Burlington is 44,019 individuals (July 1, 2025 Census data). The project will create 50 or fewer new units of housing on a tract of land involving 10 acres or less (including, at minimum, lawns, parking lots, driveways, leach fields, accessory buildings, staging areas, areas disturbed during or after construction, areas utilized as part of a shared usage (i.e., access drive or joint septic system)). The Project is further described in the JO request and exhibits (Project Number JO 4-557 on the Act 250 Database online).
